scope: Raw-candidate-aware EPIC Ego repair router and feasibility audit
summary: Ranking raw H3 as an explicit fallback did not pass held-action gates: accuracy remained 1/6 and mean regret rose to 0.0704. The feasibility audit found no repair in any of six windows that simultaneously passed background-lock 0.95 and the non-regression contract, so learned routing is rejected fail-closed.
evidence: The raw-aware experiment reports 0.1667 selection accuracy, 0.070378 mean regret, and 1.0 selected non-regression rate.
Across all six tight-support tournaments, zero candidates satisfy both background_lock >= 0.95 and non_regression.passed.
Formal evaluation therefore uses the deterministic tight-support recipe and records the learned policy as absent rather than loading a rejected checkpoint.
lessons: A learned router must not be promoted when its feasible action/background set is empty; explicit rejection is a valid optimization result.
limitations: The trained module is not deployable and does not fine-tune MiniMax-H3.
next_actions: Collect more Ego scenes and repair labels, add task-object tracking and seam supervision, and retrain before enabling learned routing.
